recordings.remarks: Recorded at Nga Manu Sanctuary at Waikanae on the Kapiti Coast. Example of part of the song range for this dialect on this section of coast, on the south-western North Island. Directly across from this location, off the coast is the large sanctuary island of Kapiti. I'm planning a trip over to the island in 2024 to see if the Kaipti Island dialect is the same as the coast dialect. I have listened to historical recordings of Tui on Kapiti Island recorded about 60 years ago. That particular dialect no longer exists anywhere in New Zealand, showing that the regional dialects change not only geographically, but over time too.
recordings.carol_category: song: harmonic 'bell' stacks (partials ~1.27 kHz apart) alternating with wheezes (Kāpiti Coast dialect)

recordings.remarks: Fights regularly start between two or more tui. Possibly over territorial disputes. They mostly end with one tui chasing another off but can get quite violent. I have seen two birds get so involved fighting that they fall out of the tree and roll around on the ground attacking each. Once, I have seen one tui kill another in such a fight, right in the middle of a city suburban street. One tui clamped it's beak around the other tui's throat, just behind the head, until it had killed the other bird. There appeared to be two separate clans of a dozen birds each, occupying separate sides of a suburban street. On one occassion, I have had a tui threaten me with swooping dive. It was clearly warning me off.
recordings.call_type_as_given: Vocalisations and wing contact made between two tui
recordings.carol_category: fight calls: rapid harmonic chatter between two tui + wing contact (aggressive/alarm-type candidate)
recordings.attribution: XC853670 by Ken George, xeno-canto.org/853670, Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0
